title: Drift-aware KV cache mixed-precision calibration and validation pipeline (INT8/FP8)
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Build and validate a repeatable calibration + validation pipeline for KV-cache mixed-precision profiles (INT8 and FP8) that is drift-aware and suitable for runtime rollouts. This ticket covers: (1) dataset and sampler selection for KV calibration, (2) automated calibration sweeps (per-layer, per-head, asymmetric vs symmetric scales), (3) accuracy validation harness for long-context regressions, (4) latency/throughput benchmarking and SLO gating, (5) rollback/fallback heuristics when drift is detected in production. This work should produce a set of calibrated profiles, an evaluation report, and a rollout playbook (canary thresholds and automatic fallback rules).
acceptance_criteria: Calib pipeline runs end-to-end and outputs profile artifacts (JSON) that the runtime can consume
Regression delta thresholds defined and enforced: median per-token logprob delta < 0.04 for FP8 and < 0.09 for INT8 on internal regression set
Latency improvement measurements for kv-traffic workload: FP8 >= 1.4x throughput vs baseline; INT8 >= 2.2x throughput vs baseline
Drift detector flags shifts in calibration distribution > 2 standard deviations and triggers autosweep job
Canary rollout config and rollback path documented and validated in staging with simulated drift scenarios
test_plan: Create calibration datasets: 10k diverse prefixes (wiki-qa-long-context), 5k instruction-style conversations (instruction-eval-1k), 2k long-dialog edge cases from customer traffic (anonymized)
Run per-layer and per-head symmetric/asymmetric calibration sweep for each folder of model checkpoints (small/medium/large)
Validate profiles using: perplexity on lm-perf-tokenized-10k, instruction-answer BLEU/ROUGE on instruction-eval-1k, and generation logprob shift on redwood-internal-regression-set
Benchmark latency/throughput under realistic prefix reuse patterns (50%, 75%, 90% cache hit ratios) and concurrency shapes (1, 4, 16)
Run staged canary in dedicated staging cluster with synthetic drift (scale perturbation and rare-token spike) to exercise fallback
experiment_results: Run A (2026-02-25): FP8 asymmetric per-layer sweep on model-xl: calibration set 10k. Result: median per-token logprob shift = 0.028; lm-perf perplexity delta +1.6%; throughput +1.45x; median p99 latency reduced from 27.2ms -> 21.9ms (19.5% reduction)

Run B (2026-03-02): INT8 symmetric per-head sweep on model-xl with 5k calibration samples. Result: median per-token logprob shift = 0.076; lm-perf perplexity delta +4.9%; throughput +2.3x; median p99 latency = 16.9ms (38% reduction). Observed occasional long-tail degradation on contexts > 2048 tokens (logprob shift up to 0.14)

Run C (2026-03-08): Mixed profile (FP8 for recent layers, INT8 for attention matrices in older layers) reduced worst-case logprob shift to 0.055 while retaining throughput +1.9x. This hybrid profile is promising for balanced latency/quality trade-offs

Drift simulation (2026-03-10): Injected token distribution skew (rare tokens up 10x). Drift detector triggered autosweep within 12 minutes; autosweep produced new profile with calibrated asymmetric scales and reduced logprob shift back to baseline within two iterations

Calibration cost: full sweep (per-layer asymmetric + per-head symmetric) with 10k samples takes ~3.6 GPU-hours on calibration harness (a single V100-equivalent); incremental autosweep (1k samples) costs ~0.4 GPU-hours
analysis_and_tradeoffs: FP8 provides a conservative quality profile: small median shifts, consistent behavior across long contexts. Best candidate for latency-sensitive apps that cannot tolerate frequent long-tail regressions
INT8 provides larger latency wins but higher tail risk on long-context or low-frequency token distributions. INT8 suitability depends on per-customer quality SLOs and presence of fallback models
Hybrid per-layer mixes enable most of INT8 throughput gains while bounding worst-case quality loss. Adds complexity to profile shipping and runtime profile selection
Calibration sample diversity matters more than absolute size beyond ~3k samples. Covering rare-token subpopulations reduces long-tail failures more effectively than pure sample count increase

Autosweep frequency vs cost: more frequent autosweeps reduce drift exposure but increase GPU spend; propose tiered policy (weekly autosweep for most customers, hourly quick-checks with smaller sample sets for high-risk customers)
next_steps: Finalize hybrid profile format and add runtime selector to map context length and cache-hit ratio to profile (FP8/INT8/hybrid)
Add deterministic unit tests for regression thresholds and integrate into CI (see PR #6241)
Schedule staged canary for model-xl hybrid profiles in dedicated staging: target date 2026-03-20
Instrument production runtime to emit calibration distribution metrics to Console (histogram of per-layer scale factors, cache hit ratios) for drift detection
Create runbook and rollback playbook and link into ops-runbooks Confluence page
